sources.code: CSS read by the Code agent on 2026-11-19 (css/components/*.css, css/site/*.css, global a rules). Updated on 2026-11-21 for Badge Danger, Link and Separator. Claude did not read the CSS; items under differences and codeOnly are Code's findings.
sources.classification: Claude's opinion, using the GOVERNANCE divergence classes: Bloqueia, Atencao, Informativo. Owner decides.

meta.policy: Figma is canonical for component values (GOVERNANCE section 7), but identity decisions in the Brandbook outrank it. Each difference below needs an owner decision: CSS follows Figma, Figma follows CSS, or accepted.

iconButton.note: Icon colour per state was not read. In code it needs an accessible name (aria-label). Not implemented in CSS.

coverage.implementedNote: Button: all 7 styles (Primary, Secondary, Ghost, Inverse, Accent and Destructive at Medium, plus Small Ghost), 4 states each (hover via :hover, focus via shared .btn:focus-visible outline, disabled via .btn.btn:disabled and per-style rules for Secondary and Ghost). Badge: Neutral, Ancora (.badge--anchor), Solar, Success, Danger (.badge--danger). Link: .link with .link--small, hover and focus-visible as pseudo-classes and disabled via aria-disabled (the global a rules are unchanged for anchors without .link). Separator: .separator.

differences.code: The new .link class matches Figma (Text/Default/Default, underline, bold on hover and focus, disabled rule). Anchors without .link, which is every anchor on the site today, still use the global a rules: Text/Brand/Default, no underline, a:hover colour and a:focus-visible with a 2px outline.
differences.measured: Link colour against surrounding text colour, Light: 3.01 against Text/Default/Default, 1.67 against Text/Default/Secondary. Dark: 1.59 and 1.28. Link colour against the page: 6.46 Light, 10.74 Dark.
differences.inference: Where a link sits inside running text coloured Text/Default/Secondary, colour alone separates it at under 3:1, which is what WCAG 1.4.1 (Use of Color, Level A) warns about. Needs a check of where links appear in running text and what a:hover does. A Brandbook rule about link style would outrank Figma.

differences.figma: Medium is 45 high, padding 12 vertical and 20 horizontal (Spacing/space-3, space-5), stroke drawn inside the box.
differences.code: Padding 11px and 19px plus the 1px border (the border is subtracted so the box matches Figma), line-height 1.6, 44px minimum height. Renders 44.8 high, 0.2 under Figma because of the line-height.
Every button is full width under 768px.

differences.figma: Caption, header and data rows are 46 high and the last row is 45; the Default table is 640 by 231 with a caption, a header and three data rows.
differences.code: Rows render 45.8 high (13px at 160% is 20.8, plus 24 of padding, plus the 1px separator) and the last row 44.8. The same table renders 230.0 high.
differences.measured: 45.8 for the caption, header and data rows, 44.8 for the last row, 276 to 640 wide as set, in the browser (Light and Dark). Under 1px per row, no decision needed.

differences.code: Class named .badge--anchor. The Figma primitives family is also Anchor.

matches: Button Medium padding 12 and 20 (border inside), radius 12, gap 8, icon 16.
Badge Neutral, Ancora, Solar, Success and Danger colour roles exist as classes. Success and Danger fills use the Figma tokens (12% and 10% in Light, solid in Dark).
Badge padding 4 and 12 and line height 160%: 28.8 high in every style, Neutral included (the 0.8px stroke is discounted from the padding), 29 in Figma.
Link: size, weight, colour, underline, focus ring (2px, 2px gap, square) and disabled weight per the Figma table.
Separator: 1px line in Border/Default/Default, full width.

Table: wrapper border, radius and background, caption, header and row header weight 500, padding 12 and 16, 1px separators except under the last row, end alignment for numeric columns, focus ring 2px with a 2px gap on the wrapper.

codeOnly.note: Solar fill button. Not the same as Figma's Accent.
Underlined link specific to the testimonial card.
